Imagine looking in the mirror, and your skin has gone completely clear.
You'd think you'd turn invisible, like a ghost.
But skin is only a thin wrapper.
Underneath, you'd see bright red muscles, yellow fat, and blood rushing through your veins.
Skin looks solid because its cells bounce light around, like fog, and its pigment soaks some up.
That pigment is your built-in sunscreen.
Without it, sunlight could burn you far more easily.
Glass frogs live like this, and hide their blood in their liver when they sleep.
And scientists have already made a mouse's skin see-through, for a little while, using yellow food dye.
So in the mirror, you wouldn't vanish. You'd see everything you're made of.
